extractor_notes: The 2012 codified Sec. 201.40(b) text spans PDF pages 19-20 (txt lines 3731-3974) and contains 8 granted classes, matching INDEX.md's expected count of 8. The 2012 Final Rule uses the modern style: each class is a single complex sentence with nested conditional clauses (e.g., 'where circumvention is accomplished solely in order to ...'), so permitted_uses[] and exclusions[] were decomposed from those conditional phrases. Notable structural points: classes (b)(4) and (b)(5) are parallel (DVD/CSS vs. online distribution services) and both restrict circumvention to short portions for criticism/comment in four enumerated contexts (noncommercial videos, documentary films, nonfiction multimedia ebooks offering film analysis, and educational purposes in film studies or other courses requiring close analysis); classes (b)(6) and (b)(7) are the parallel screen-capture variants of (b)(4)/(b)(5) and were granted as separate alternative exemptions; class (b)(3) (wireless handset unlocking) is unusual for limiting eligibility to handsets 'originally acquired ... no later than ninety days after the effective date of this exemption'; class (b)(8) is a research-and-development exemption for assistive-player development (blind/visually impaired/deaf/hard of hearing). There is no separate (c) Definitions section in 2012; definitions ('noncommercial videos') are embedded inside the relevant class.

exemptions.equipment_or_work: Literary works distributed electronically with TPMs blocking read-aloud or screen readers
permitted_uses: Circumvention when a copy of such a work is lawfully obtained by a blind or other person with a disability, as such a person is defined in 17 U.S.C. 121
Circumvention when such work is a nondramatic literary work, lawfully obtained and used by an authorized entity pursuant to 17 U.S.C. 121
exclusions: Limited to literary works distributed electronically that are protected by technological measures which either prevent the enabling of read-aloud functionality or interfere with screen readers or other applications or assistive technologies

For the disabled-individual prong, requires that the rights owner is remunerated, as appropriate, for the price of the mainstream copy of the work as made available to the general public through customary channels
For the authorized-entity prong, the work must be a nondramatic literary work and use must be pursuant to 17 U.S.C. 121
definitions_or_conditions: 'Blind or other person with a disability' is defined by reference to 17 U.S.C. 121
'Authorized entity' is defined by reference to 17 U.S.C. 121

source.quote: (1) Literary works, distributed electronically, that are protected by technological measures which either prevent the enabling of read-aloud functionality or interfere with screen readers or other applications or assistive technologies in the following instances: (i) When a copy of such a work is lawfully obtained by a blind or other person with a disability, as such a person is defined in 17 U.S.C. 121; provided, however, the rights owner is remunerated, as appropriate, for the price of the mainstream copy of the work as made available to the general public through customary channels; or (ii) When such work is a nondramatic literary work, lawfully obtained and used by an authorized entity pursuant to 17 U.S.C. 121.

exemptions.equipment_or_work: Computer programs enabling wireless telephone handsets to execute lawfully obtained software applications (jailbreaking)
permitted_uses: Circumvention of computer programs that enable wireless telephone handsets to execute lawfully obtained software applications, for the sole purpose of enabling interoperability of such applications with computer programs on the telephone handset
exclusions: Circumvention must be accomplished for the sole purpose of enabling interoperability of lawfully obtained software applications with computer programs on the telephone handset
definitions_or_conditions: Applies to computer programs that enable wireless telephone handsets to execute lawfully obtained software applications

source.quote: (2) Computer programs that enable wireless telephone handsets to execute lawfully obtained software applications, where circumvention is accomplished for the sole purpose of enabling interoperability of such applications with computer programs on the telephone handset.

exemptions.equipment_or_work: Computer programs (firmware/software) enabling wireless telephone handsets acquired no later than 90 days after effective date to connect to a different network (handset unlocking)
permitted_uses: Circumvention of firmware or software that enables a wireless telephone handset to connect to a different wireless telecommunications network, when initiated by the owner (an individual consumer who is also the owner of the copy of the computer program in the handset), solely in order to connect to a different wireless telecommunications network, and where such access to the network is authorized by the operator of the network
exclusions: Limited to wireless telephone handsets originally acquired from the operator of a wireless telecommunications network or retailer no later than ninety days after the effective date of this exemption
Only available if the operator of the wireless communications network to which the handset is locked has failed to unlock it within a reasonable period of time following a request by the owner
Circumvention must be initiated by the owner, an individual consumer, who is also the owner of the copy of the computer program in such wireless telephone handset
Circumvention must be undertaken solely in order to connect to a different wireless telecommunications network
Such access to the network must be authorized by the operator of the network
definitions_or_conditions: The handset must have been originally acquired from the operator of a wireless telecommunications network or retailer
The owner-consumer must also be the owner of the copy of the computer program in the handset

source.quote: (3) Computer programs, in the form of firmware or software, that enable a wireless telephone handset originally acquired from the operator of a wireless telecommunications network or retailer no later than ninety days after the effective date of this exemption to connect to a different wireless telecommunications network, if the operator of the wireless communications network to which the handset is locked has failed to unlock it within a reasonable period of time following a request by the owner of the wireless telephone handset, and when circumvention is initiated by the owner, an individual consumer, who is also the owner of the copy of the computer program in such wireless telephone handset, solely in order to connect to a different wireless telecommunications network, and such access to the network is authorized by the operator of the network.

exemptions.equipment_or_work: Motion pictures on DVDs protected by CSS, for short-portion criticism/comment uses
permitted_uses: Circumvention to make use of short portions of motion pictures for the purpose of criticism or comment in noncommercial videos
Circumvention to make use of short portions of motion pictures for the purpose of criticism or comment in documentary films
Circumvention to make use of short portions of motion pictures for the purpose of criticism or comment in nonfiction multimedia ebooks offering film analysis

Circumvention to make use of short portions of motion pictures for educational purposes in film studies or other courses requiring close analysis of film and media excerpts, by college and university faculty, college and university students, and kindergarten through twelfth grade educators
exclusions: Limited to motion pictures, as defined in 17 U.S.C. 101, on DVDs that are lawfully made and acquired and that are protected by the Content Scrambling System

The person engaging in circumvention must believe and have reasonable grounds for believing that circumvention is necessary because reasonably available alternatives, such as noncircumventing methods or using screen capture software as provided for in alternative exemptions, are not able to produce the level of high-quality content required to achieve the desired criticism or comment
Circumvention must be undertaken solely in order to make use of short portions of the motion pictures for the purpose of criticism or comment
Use must fall within one of the four enumerated instances (noncommercial videos, documentary films, nonfiction multimedia ebooks offering film analysis, or specified educational purposes)
definitions_or_conditions: 'Motion pictures' is defined by reference to 17 U.S.C. 101
'Noncommercial videos' includes videos created pursuant to a paid commission, provided that the commissioning entity's use is noncommercial

source.quote: (4) Motion pictures, as defined in 17 U.S.C. 101, on DVDs that are lawfully made and acquired and that are protected by the Content Scrambling System, where the person engaging in circumvention believes and has reasonable grounds for believing that circumvention is necessary because reasonably available alternatives, such as noncircumventing methods or using screen capture software as provided for in alternative exemptions, are not able to produce the level of high-quality content required to achieve the desired criticism or comment on such motion pictures, and where circumvention is undertaken solely in order to make use of short portions of the motion pictures for the purpose of criticism or comment in the following instances: (i) In noncommercial videos; (ii) In documentary films; (iii) In nonfiction multimedia ebooks offering film analysis; and (iv) For educational purposes in film studies or other courses requiring close analysis of film and media excerpts, by college and university faculty, college and university students, and kindergarten through twelfth grade educators. For purposes of this exemption, ''noncommercial videos'' includes videos created pursuant to a paid commission, provided that the commissioning entity's use is noncommercial.

exemptions.equipment_or_work: Motion pictures and other audiovisual works on CSS-protected DVDs or distributed by an online service, for accessibility-player research and development
permitted_uses: Circumvention accomplished solely to access the playhead and/or related time code information embedded in copies of such works, and solely for the purpose of conducting research and development for the purpose of creating players capable of rendering visual representations of the audible portions of such works and/or audible representations or descriptions of the visual portions of such works, to enable an individual who is blind, visually impaired, deaf, or hard of hearing, and who has lawfully obtained a copy of such a work, to perceive the work
exclusions: Limited to motion pictures and other audiovisual works on DVDs that are protected by the Content Scrambling System, or that are distributed by an online service and protected by technological measures that control access to such works
Circumvention must be accomplished solely to access the playhead and/or related time code information embedded in copies of such works

Circumvention must be solely for the purpose of conducting research and development for creating players to enable blind, visually impaired, deaf, or hard-of-hearing individuals (who have lawfully obtained a copy) to perceive the work
The resulting player must not require circumvention of technological measures to operate
definitions_or_conditions: The end user enabled by the resulting player must be an individual who is blind, visually impaired, deaf, or hard of hearing, and who has lawfully obtained a copy of such a work
The resulting player must be capable of rendering visual representations of the audible portions of such works and/or audible representations or descriptions of the visual portions of such works

source.quote: (8) Motion pictures and other audiovisual works on DVDs that are protected by the Content Scrambling System, or that are distributed by an online service and protected by technological measures that control access to such works, when circumvention is accomplished solely to access the playhead and/or related time code information embedded in copies of such works and solely for the purpose of conducting research and development for the purpose of creating players capable of rendering visual representations of the audible portions of such works and/or audible representations or descriptions of the visual portions of such works to enable an individual who is blind, visually impaired, deaf, or hard of hearing, and who has lawfully obtained a copy of such a work, to perceive the work; provided however, that the resulting player does not require circumvention of technological measures to operate.
